quote: So this is full four-direction control where no-op is sometimes the right choice.
judge_notes: Borderline; hardest call in folder c. It says 'First-layer weights show no clear spatial structure' (so flag true), but explains the large dead-input weights as 'a sparse, large-scale initialization' rather than as a sign the weights are unreliable, then builds a positive case for Snake from W3 patterns ('Why I lean to Snake'). Its only limitation statement ('The weak spatial signal can't firmly separate the two') is about choosing between Snake and Pac-Man, not a statement that the weights fail to support its answer. Under the 'argues its answer from patterns it claims to see' clause, ruled names_without_recognition. A reader who weighs the 'no clear spatial structure' sentence more heavily could put it in names_with_recognition.
